newsitem.title: FRANCE: Alcatel CIT sees breakeven in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Alcatel CIT sees breakeven in 1998.

text.p: Alcatel Alsthom's telecommunications equipment subsidiary Alcatel CIT expects to break even next year, Alcatel CIT managing director Gerard Dega said on Monday.
"If the jobs plan goes smoothly, 1997 will still show a loss but a reduced one...In 1998, we should have recovered to breakeven," Dega told a news conference.

Alcatel CIT lost between 400 million and 500 million francs in 1996 and was also in the red at the operating level. Although Alcatel CIT had a similar net loss in 1995, it was profitable at the operating level, Dega said.
Turnover fell two percent in 1996 to just over 11 billion francs, due in part to a drop in orders from France Telecom, he said.

Dega said he was optimistic given the brisk development of infrastructure for mobile phones. "That activity accounted for close to 27 percent of 1996 business. It should reach 40 percent this year," he said.
The group in September put the number of excess staff at 1,636 in a report detailing its economic situation. It revised the figure to 1,206 in a jobs plan presented last month to the staff council.
The plan entails 1,511 departures and 305 hires over this year and next. Provisions for the plan were taken in the 1995 and 1996 results and will have no impact on this year's results, Dega said.
